Jordan — thanks for the recap and recording. Good summary. A few follow-ups from our infra team so we can prep internal requirements before Thu: 

1) 429 handling: for our search service we expect bursty traffic (indexing cycles + user queries). Do you have recommended client-side behavior for 429s beyond exponential backoff? Is there a recommended header pattern we should emit to help your routing layer make better decisions?

2) Idempotency: For generation endpoints we want exactly-once behavior for certain billing-sensitive flows. Does the SDK support idempotency keys / request IDs natively, and what are best practices when you have async retries across a retry proxy?

3) Auth: we use short-lived tokens from our internal STS. How does Redwood handle token rotation in long-lived SDK processes (e.g., worker pools), and are there hooks for automated refresh?

4) Embeddings + reranker: we need guidance on batch sizes vs latency. Target SLO is 200ms P95 for the reranker at 500 QPS sustained. Any data or recommendations you can share before the call would help.

If you can send the SDK snippet and the X-Request-ID / retry pattern before EOD that would be great. Also confirm Thu 12/2 10am PT works for your team.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Hi Sophie — quick technical notes and a few concrete recommendations. I’ll walk through these during the deep-dive and paste runnable snippets into the shared Drive; attaching a short text file with the auth/snippet examples now (sdk-auth-snippets.txt).

1) 429 handling + client guidance- Use standard exponential backoff with full jitter (base=200ms, cap=8s). For bursty workloads we recommend an adaptive short-circuit: if X-RateLimit-Reset header indicates > 1s, escalate delay to header-provided reset.
- When retrying, include X-Request-ID and X-RW-Retry-Count headers so our routing/telemetry can correlate attempts.
- Server-side we provide a quota header set: X-RW-Quota-Remaining and X-RW-Quota-Window to allow clients to implement soft-fails before hard 429s.

2) Idempotency & request IDs- Recommendation: attach a client-generated UUID in header X-Request-ID for every user-facing request. For mutating/generation calls that are billing-sensitive, also set Idempotency-Key header for server-side deduplication (we persist idempotency keys for 24h by default, configurable for enterprises).
- If you have a retry proxy between client and Redwood, make sure the proxy preserves X-Request-ID and Idempotency-Key across retries.

3) Auth and token rotation- SDK supports pluggable auth providers and exposes a refresh hook: set a token provider that returns a short-lived token; SDK will call the hook on 401 and attempt one transparent refresh+retry. For worker pools, implement a token cache keyed by worker id and listen for 401 to force refresh.

4) Embeddings batching & reranker latency- For 200ms P95 at 500 QPS we recommend:
  - Embeddings: batch size 64–128 depending on average vector size, prioritize async batching for throughput, stream partial responses if you need lower p50.
  - Reranker: run the lightweight reranker in a two-stage pipeline: candidate generation (embedding similarity) then a compact reranker model for final scoring. Use model sharding and request affinitized routing to keep KV cache hot.

5) Routing, fallbacks and costs- Configure routing policy to prefer low-latency endpoints for user-facing queries and fall back to cost-optimized variants on overloads. We support auto-fallback policies that drop into a cached-response tier for cold startup windows.

Example header snippet (pseudo):

curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <SHORT_LIVED_TOKEN>" \
  -H "X-Request-ID: 7f9b3e2a-9a8f-4d2a-bc1f-1a2b3c4d5e6f" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: user123-session-20271130" \
  -d '{"prompt":"..."}'

Retry strategy (pseudocode):
- attempt = 0
- while attempt < 6:
    wait = min(8000, base * 2^attempt) * random(0,1)
    sleep(wait)
    attempt += 1

Notes: include both X-Request-ID and Idempotency-Key. We’ll surface traces in the console when those headers are present.

I’ll prepare a short runbook page covering: header mappings, quota header semantics, and sample SDK code for token refresh and request-id generation.

Marissa
